related_questions.question: What are the odds of surviving lung cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: The chance of surviving lung cancer varies significantly based on the stage and type of cancer at diagnosis, as well as individual factors like age and overall health. Generally, survival rates are higher for early-stage lung cancer and can be significantly lower for later stages. The five-year survival rate for all stages combined is around 25.4%.
snippet_highlighted_words: The five-year survival rate for all stages combined is around 25.4%

list.title: Early-stage (Localized):
list.snippet: Lung cancer that is confined to the lung has a much higher survival rate. For example, around 65% of people with stage 1 lung cancer survive five years or more, according to Cancer Research UK.

list.title: Later-stage (Regional and Distant):
list.snippet: Survival rates drop significantly as the cancer spreads to lymph nodes (regional) or other organs (distant). For instance, stage 4 lung cancer has a five-year survival rate of around 5%, according to Cancer Research UK.

list.title: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC):
list.snippet: This is the most common type of lung cancer. Survival rates vary by stage, but overall, the five-year survival rate for NSCLC is higher than for small cell lung cancer.

list.title: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC):
list.snippet: SCLC is more aggressive and has a lower overall five-year survival rate, around 8.6%.
Early Diagnosis: Catching lung cancer early significantly improves survival chances.
Treatment: The type of treatment received (surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, etc.) also plays a crucial role in survival.
Individual Health: Factors like age, overall health, and performance status can influence survival.

text_blocks.snippet: Lung cancer survival rates are complex and depend on multiple factors. While the overall five-year survival rate is around 25.4%, survival can range from very high for early-stage NSCLC to very low for late-stage SCLC.
